**Performance: pass-with-notes** at `5aee7a1032123a10e49dd007ac88681fcba94fa8`. **P152-F001, P152-F002 and P152-F003 are closed.**

Delta review only, `253374c..5aee7a1`: merge `e83e1de` brings main `cee0113` and its previously reviewed costs; runtime repairs are `d8634d6`, and `5aee7a1` adds canary/acceptance receipts only. Earlier qualifications stand except those superseded below. No local builds, tests, probes, model calls or canary reruns.

## Closure and actual resource shape

**P152-F001 closed: scope precedes the page limit.** `store/src/held.rs:41-63` restricts both union arms to the supplied recipient array before ORDER/LIMIT. The ended-hold arm searches the recipient/job partial unflagged index; the live-job arm uses `jobs_serial` (serial_key, state), selecting pending/running rows rather than terminal history. Ack/flag inserts persist recipient from the job. Empty fleet skips even the schema read.

The regression creates **60 older completed foreign holds plus 60 older queued foreign holds**, returns the one local hold, flags it once and verifies foreign held rows remain unflagged. CI also executes the EXPLAIN guard. This proves the starvation repair, not constant cost: fleet serialization/JSON-list processing scales with fleet bytes; candidate reads/joins, JSON extraction and ordering scale with that fleet's unflagged holds/live jobs. LIMIT 50 bounds the returned page, not all local candidate work. The stale "constant per digest / two partial indexes" source comment is not the cost model.

**P152-F002 closed: one terminal watcher, not one per steer.** `store.mjs:1580-1624` starts one owner's `waitForCompletion`, then attaches consumed later completions to its shared promise and reports each separately at the observed end. Live events also reach the owner when the foreground completion changes. Failure clears shared settling references so a later caller can retry; RPC deadline/receiver-stop behavior remains.

The **six-steer test** acknowledges all seven messages, asserts one `completion-wait`, prevents additional untriggered run-state questions during the running interval, then checks every completion is reported once and the end costs at most two processing questions. Individual injection, journal acceptance, native consumption and ACK paths remain separate.

Terminal history/run-state polling is now constant in unfinished-message count: one owner's history cursor/backoff (250 ms rising to five seconds), one queue/processing snapshot per trigger or 30-second re-ask, with existing 15-second SDK-call deadline timers. Foreground consumption/baseline/discard checks still add per-message work and can overlap that observer; this is not one total SDK read per seat.

**P152-N001, retention qualifier:** correlation/member state and terminal reporting remain **O(J)** for J steers. Successful `turnWatch` retains its members until replaced or the bridge is collected; no success-path clear or hard member-count cap was added. Terminal reporting can burst J records synchronously. This does not reopen the poller-fanout finding, but idle RSS and many-steer state retention should be measured; clearing an already-reported watch is the smallest potential follow-up.

**P152-F003 closed: the busy claim has no 500 ms tick.** `delivery/mod.rs:1687-1695,1961-1970` subscribes to recipient-filtered enqueue/outcome and `steer.changed` events, with the named **15-second backstop** for timed retries. No global-event wake fanout. The old native 500 ms wait remains only outside the during-turn path.

In a quiet uninterrupted claim, the backstop contributes about **0.067 loop wakes/s**, versus **2/s** on the old native timer. Events and HTTP deadline/retry renewals add work, and each loop wake performs recipient/lease/claim checks. This is one timer per waiting claim, normally one foreground claim per native bridge, not a daemon-enforced global one-per-seat cap. A timed retry can wait up to the backstop interval plus processing delay when no event wakes it.

The switch is additionally read at a claimed job's handoff: schema check plus primary-key setting query, with the existing global native guard held through that awaited read. If off, the job is retried/released and the receiver gets turn-wait. No switch read was added to every empty-loop tick. The HTTP request's initial switch lookup and deadline renewal still mean "per claim" is not "only per message."

## What 44-to-4 proves

The author reports **44 recipient reads versus 4 over ten simulated idle seconds** in `a_during_turn_wait_wakes_on_events_and_rechecks_the_switch_at_hand_off`. It uses a **paused Tokio clock, fake registry/queue and an injected atomic switch**, not a live daemon measurement.

Exact-head CI executes assertions of **native reads >=30 and during-turn reads <=4**, plus event-driven delivery after the switch changes and proof the job stays queued. The old-mode comparison is a positive control for the counting instrument. Passing output does not independently record the exact 44; it verifies the asserted bounds. Ten seconds is shorter than the new backstop, so this case does not measure its steady-state rate, SQL/CPU/RSS, HTTP renewals or deadline delivery.

## Other delta costs and proof limits

Role-correlated replies add a request lookup before send, existing caller resolution, and the original lookup/idempotent answer transaction after successful send. Pane resolution can list the roster and probe matching process identities; an unresolved pane can invoke existing session-record diagnostics. Normal readable native-process checks launch nothing, but those reused liveness paths retain the counted absolute-ps fallback on unanswered kernel evidence. Thus **no new executable launch site** does not mean every reply path has zero inherited launches.

A newly stamped answer attempts one additional awaited spine append/publication, including its ordering-lock wait, owned task, payload bytes and broadcast. Replay may still pay the no-change answer transaction but does not append again. **The append is best-effort after stamping:** a failed append logs and does not roll back answered_at. That limits any "every answer is durably audited" claim; the authority/audit conditions were handed to security, not certified by this cost pass.

The refreshed canary is a real CLI **1.0.108-1** host/extension and private daemon/store at runtime source `d8634d6`, using **deterministic local fixture inference**, not a real provider. Its five steer **claim-to-ACK times are 4/8/10/10/10 s**, while **queue-to-ACK times are 4/8/12/16/20 s**. Off-case queue-to-ACK is **83 s**. These confirm the documented fixture pacing and non-wedge behavior, not production latency/billing or exactly one additional billable request per steer.

**CI:** CLEAN at the exact head. [CI 42378488326](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42378488326) succeeds in all four jobs; JUnit records **2,089 executed cases, zero failures/errors**, including scoped held-page, index, event-wait and all six spawn guards; five Rust tests are skipped separately. Node 22 native gate: **328/328 pass**, including shared watcher and steered-abort recovery. Node 24 check also succeeds. Latest delivers **42378515919** succeeds; the earlier delivers attempt **42378488327 was cancelled**, not passed. Author-reported mutation failures were not rerun here.

Migration 0038 remains above current main's schema 36. Under the prime's merge-order rule, a later merge after a higher-numbered migration must renumber and preserve the compiled schema maximum; SQLx's ability to apply absent lower versions does not waive that rule.

**After deploy, AC1/AC7 still owed:** matched same-PID/build launch sites and machine rate; daemon/extension CPU/RSS; busy-empty-inbox claim/SQL rate including backstop and HTTP renewals; SDK history/queue/processing rates and outstanding observer count versus steers; per-message correlation retention, and queue-to-claim/claim-to-ACK distributions including stalled/failed work. Use authorized normal traffic, not a synthetic load storm. Source/paused-clock proof is not a live cost reading.
